attempted_claim: Let G be the free step-3 rank-2 Cartan group with left-invariant rank-2 distribution D from the identity e, and let Abn(e) be the set of endpoints of all nonconstant D-horizontal abnormal curves starting at e (critical values of the endpoint map). Prove or disprove that Abn(e) is contained in a proper analytic (in fact algebraic) subvariety of G of codimension at least 2, given by explicit polynomial equations in exponential coordinates, and hence has 5-dimensional Lebesgue measure zero. Scope is all abnormal curves from e, any length. A complete answer must either prove containment with stated explicit equations and codimension bound with Sard-type measure conclusion, or exhibit a nonempty open subset of G contained in Abn(e) or explicit abnormal endpoints violating every such proper-subvariety containment of the stated codimension.
claim_type: containment of abnormal set in explicit codimension-2 algebraic subvariety
decisive_failure: originality: FAIL: the exact determination was already published by Ardentov-Le Donne-Sachkov (arXiv:1810.03869, 2018; Steklov Proc. 2019) Theorem 3, which proves abnormal trajectories of the Cartan rank-2 step-3 group are exactly the one-parameter subgroups tangent to span(X1,X2) with projections to the (x,y)-plane straight lines and explicit parametrization x=u1*t, y=u2*t, z=0, v=u2*(u1^2+u2^2)/6*t^3, w=-u1*(u1^2+u2^2)/6*t^3, i.e. manifold A={z=0,v=y(x^2+y^2)/6,w=-x(x^2+y^2)/6}. Up to the polynomial change between their graded coordinates and first-kind exponential coordinates, A is exactly the plane {x3=x4=x5=0}: both are the union of the same horizontal one-parameter subgroups, both cut out by three polynomial equations of codimension 3. The collinearity lemma (u orthogonal to fixed (h4,h5)) and endpoint set are therefore mechanically implied; restating them in first-kind coordinates with the measure-zero corollary is a recomputation/certificate/repackaging of a known stronger classification, not a new claim. A timestamp or failed literal-title search does not establish priority.
